Each cell of a grid carries two quantities, $u$ and $v$.

$\Delta u$ measures how much $u$ differs from the mean of its neighbours: it is the diffusion, which tends to even everything out.

The term $u\,v^2$ is the reaction: $v$ is manufactured at the expense of $u$, and the more $v$ there is, the faster. $F$ replenishes $u$ from outside and $k$ removes $v$.

The subscript 2 warns that this number is written in base 2, not in the usual one. It is read digit by digit: “zero, one, one, zero, one, one, one, zero”, never “one million one hundred and one thousand…”.

How it is obtained: you keep subtracting the largest power of two that fits. Does 128 fit in 110? No, so first digit 0. Does 64 fit? Yes, 46 is left, digit 1. Does 32 fit? Yes, 14 is left, digit 1. 16? No, digit 0. 8? Yes, 6 is left, digit 1. 4? Yes, 2 is left, digit 1. 2? Yes, 0 is left, digit 1. 1? No, digit 0.

And those eight digits are the rule: they say whether the cell ends up on for each of the eight possible neighbourhoods.
